title: Kitten Swarm Linear Algebra 001
research_question: Can a large population of tiny matrix workers plus cheap probabilistic verification and selective recomputation reproduce an exact matrix product while reducing each worker's local compute and residency contract?

source_relatives.work: Freivalds, Probabilistic Machines Can Use Less Running Time
Drineas, Kannan, Mahoney, Fast Monte Carlo Algorithms for Matrices I: Approximating Matrix Multiplication
Strohmer and Vershynin, A Randomized Kaczmarz Algorithm with Exponential Convergence
source_relatives.role: small-random-subproblem worker relative for later KSLA lane

source_relatives.work: Dutta et al., On the Optimal Recovery Threshold of Coded Matrix Multiplication
source_relatives.role: coded-worker / straggler-tolerance relative for later KSLA lane

novelty_boundary: The experiment composes established block matrix multiplication and Freivalds-style verification with explicit weak-worker contracts, selective recomputation, finite-residency accounting, and a future precision-escalation ladder. It does not claim invention of the underlying algorithms.
nonclaims: No real distributed cluster is benchmarked.
Injected worker faults are synthetic and are not a measured error rate for low-precision arithmetic or small language models.
The scale model counts arithmetic and working-set proxies, not wall-clock speed, energy, or network contention.
The finite-field exact fixture is not yet a floating-point numerical-stability result.
The design does not claim invention of Freivalds verification, block matrix multiplication, randomized Kaczmarz, or coded matrix multiplication.
